your_book:
Wednesday was a split session for Jaleel's book — software carried the day while space and semiconductors dragged. ServiceNow (+4.65%, now +21.5% overall) and Adobe (+5.72%, +7.4%) were the standout movers, both riding a sector rotation trade as investors pivoted from AI hardware into software names ahead of Microsoft's post-close earnings. SAP added another +3.81% on the same tailwind. That software surge is what kept the book's unrealized gain at $232 on a $22,757 account — without it, the session would have looked considerably uglier.

The real damage came from Rocket Lab, which shed another 8.28% and now sits 25.2% in the hole on a $2,930 position — the largest single drag in the book and flagged AVOID with a QARP of 49.3, the lowest quality score here. That's a thesis-vs-price divergence that's hard to ignore: Jaleel is still holding a position the model rates avoid while it bleeds. NVIDIA slipped 3.55% (QARP 84.0, STRONG BUY) — the semiconductor selloff looks like rotation noise rather than deterioration, but the export-control overhang is real and earnings loom August 26. Boston Scientific is essentially flat on the day but its next catalyst is today (July 29 earnings) after FY26 guidance was already slashed from 10.5% to 7–8.5% growth — that read matters immediately.

Watch the drift in LULU (-1.07%, -6.9% total) and SPGI (-1.11%, -6.1% total) — both are underwater on the position with ongoing fundamental headwinds (guidance cut and tariff margin pressure for LULU; a small position but six points in the red for SPGI). The software pop today is a sentiment trade, not a fundamental re-rating; if Microsoft's print disappoints after the close, NOW and ADBE could give back a chunk of today's gains quickly.

attention.headline: AVOID-rated, down 25.2% — another 8.28% today with no thesis support
attention.note: At nearly 13% of the book, Rocket Lab is the single largest position and carries the lowest QARP score (49.3) with an AVOID verdict; the continued price deterioration against a negative model rating is a direct contradiction of a capital-preservation mandate that demands a decision, not patience.

attention.headline: Earnings catalyst is today — guidance already slashed, flat through Q3 guided
attention.note: Boston Scientific's next catalyst date is July 29 (today), and management has already pre-guided flat growth through Q3 after cutting FY26 targets from 10.5% to 7–8.5%; Jaleel needs to know the actual print before the next session to decide whether the STRONG BUY thesis still holds or the flag escalates.

attention.headline: Guidance-cut risk flag, -6.9% on position, Americas comps negative five straight quarters
attention.note: Lululemon carries an elevated risk flag with deteriorating fundamentals (tariff margin hit, China stall, fifth consecutive negative Americas comp) and the position is nearly 7% underwater — the next read on whether comps stabilize isn't until September 2.

attention.headline: Semiconductor rotation selloff (-3.55%) meets export-control overhang ahead of Aug 26 earnings
attention.note: Today's drop looks like sector rotation noise but the China export-license tightening and Senate scrutiny flagged in the risk data are structural headwinds that won't resolve before the August 26 earnings print, making this worth monitoring closely despite the STRONG BUY rating.
